results.title: UN Security Council adopts resolution on digital threats to children in conflict
results.description: NEW YORK — The UN Security Council unanimously adopted a resolution on Monday addressing how digital technologies are used to commit violations and abuses against children in armed conflict. The resolution, penned by Greece, also stressed the need to provide children with digital literacy so they can identify online risks and help prevent violations before they occur. The measure urged member states to improve domestic compliance with their obligations under international law to end and prevent violations and abuses against children, including those committed, facilitated or amplified through digital technologies. Greece chaired the Working Group on Children and Armed Conflict in 2025. Speaking before the vote, Greece's UN envoy Aglaia Balta said the Council must not stay silent on the digital dimension of grave violations."The question before us is not whether the Council should address the digital dimension of grave violations, but whether it can afford to remain silent while others exploit it," she said. Balta stressed that the resolution reinforces the existing framework by ensuring it captures violations regardless of the means used."Recruitment through a smartphone is still recruitment. A mandate that cannot see where violations begin is a mandate that falls behind," she said. Describing the text as a starting point, Balta said: "This resolution does not close the chapter on this urgent issue; it opens it. It is a seed, one that must grow as digital technologies reshape every aspect of human life, and above all, the lives of children.""Thirty years ago, the international community resolved that children caught in war would no longer be invisible. Today, we must make sure they do not vanish in the digital space," she added. Vanessa Frazier, UN Special Representative for Children and Armed Conflict, welcomed the decision, following the 15-member Council’s unanimous approval of the draft resolution.“I would like to thank the members of the Security Council and the international community for their continued engagement and support on the issue of children affected by armed conflict,” Frazier said. “Today’s resolution provides an important step to better respond to the needs of boys and girls, including by strengthening efforts to ensure their safety and well-being in an increasingly digital world and ensuring that every child can benefit from digital opportunities without being exposed to harm,” she added.

results.title: 2679 مختصًا سعوديًا يقودون 51% من الخدمات البيئية بالمملكة
results.description: كشف المركز الوطني للرقابة على الالتزام البيئي، أن الكوادر السعودية شكلت 51% من إجمالي العاملين بمقدمي الخدمات البيئية في المستويات العليا والمتوسطة، ليبلغ عددهم 2679 مختصاً يعملون لدى 485 جهة مرخصة في المملكة. وأوضح المركز أنه أصدر 43 ترخيصاً جديداً خلال الربع الثالث من عام 2026، ليرتفع إجمالي التراخيص المصدرة منذ بداية العام إلى 123 ترخيصاً. فيما تم تجديد 23 ترخيصاً بعد استيفاء المتطلبات الفنية والإدارية خلال الفترة ذاتها. أهم التعديلات المُنفذة وبينت بيانات المركز إجراء تعديلات على 110 تراخيص قائمة؛ شملت تحديث بيانات الكوادر الفنية، ورفع تصنيف جهات استشارية بعد استيفائها المعايير. وتضمنت التعديلات إضافة أجهزة بيئية متخصصة لتعزيز القدرات الفنية والتشغيلية للمرخصين. وأشارت البيانات إلى أن 51% من مقدمي الخدمات البيئية باتوا يعتمدون بالكامل على الكفاءات الوطنية. ويغطي المختصون السعوديون مجالات فنية تتضمن: الاستشارات والدراسات البيئية، الرصد والقياس، وتقييم الأثر البيئي، بما يدعم الأنشطة الاقتصادية والتنموية. وتهدف منظومة التراخيص إلى ضمان استيفاء مقدمي الخدمات للمتطلبات التنظيمية والفنية، وتطوير قدراتهم المهنية؛ بما يسهم في رفع كفاءة الجهات العاملة، وتعزيز جودة الخدمات البيئية المقدمة للقطاعين الحكومي والخاص.

results.title: ATMOCE Extends Australian M-ELV 7 kWh Battery Warranty to 15 Years
results.description: New 15-year warranty covers all MS-7K-U units already shipped to Australia SYDNEY, Oct. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- ATMOCE Australia and New Zealand has extended the standard Australian warranty for its M-ELV 7 kWh Battery (MS-7K-U) from 12 to 15 years. ATMOCE M-ELV Battery Installed at a Residential Property in Melbourne The new warranty provides 15 years or 29.2 MWh of energy throughput, with a minimum of 60% SOH retained, whichever comes first. It applies Australia-wide without regional restrictions and extends to all MS-7K-U units already shipped to Australia. The warranty extension applies across Australia, including to customers who have already purchased the applicable products. The 15-year warranty period is calculated from the original warranty start date. The change places ATMOCE in the longest standard-warranty tier in the Australian residential battery market, backed by 29.2 MWh of warranted energy throughput. The extension comes as ATMOCE approaches its first anniversary in Australia and prepares to showcase the next stage of its Extra-Low Voltage energy platform at All Energy Australia 2026 in Melbourne later this month. "Extending the MS-7K-U warranty to 15 years is another step in our commitment to the Australian market," said Zebb Wilson, Sales Director at ATMOCE ANZ. "It reflects the confidence we have in the technology and gives customers and industry partners greater certainty around the long-term value of the system. As we continue to invest in product development and long-term system performance, we want the support behind our products to reflect that same commitment." Designed for Long-Term Residential Energy Storage The MS-7K-U is built around ATMOCE's Extra-Low Voltage architecture, operating at 25.6 V DC, and uses an AC-coupled design suited to both new installations and retrofit applications. The architecture supports single- and three-phase systems and integration with third-party photovoltaic (PV) inverters, giving installers greater flexibility when designing or upgrading residential energy systems. For installers and channel partners, the warranty extension provides additional certainty when discussing system longevity, product support and whole-of-life value with customers. "Warranty is increasingly part of the conversations installers are having with customers," said Grant Behrendorff, Managing Director and Co-Founder at AC Solar Warehouse. "Moving to 15 years gives installers greater confidence in the long-term proposition they are putting in front of homeowners." Safety Backed by Independent Fire Testing The extended warranty sits alongside ATMOCE's focus on safety at the system architecture level. The MS-7K-U has undergone independent fire testing. During testing, one battery cell was forced to 233 °C and ignited, with the test recording no explosion, no pack-wide thermal runaway and no gas released outside the battery enclosure. The battery uses lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cells supported by three layers of protection: intrinsic, passive and active. Intrinsic protection begins with the system's 25.6 V nominal Extra-Low Voltage DC architecture, with a fire-suppression device designed to activate at approximately 170 °C while active protection monitors voltage, current, temperature and insulation. Together, these measures are designed to provide multiple layers of protection throughout system operation. ATMOCE Returns to All Energy Australia ATMOCE will return to All Energy Australia 2026 at Booth EE101, Melbourne Convention and Exhibition Centre, 28–29 October, showcasing its Extra-Low Voltage technology platform and joining industry partners for sessions on safety, system simplicity, Virtual Power Plant (VPP) participation and interoperability. Sessions will include Glen Morris and OpenSolar addressing Smart Energy Council Installer Roadshow FAQs and system design, a discussion on safer and simpler solar storage for New Zealand, and a session with AC Solar Warehouse exploring what installers need from battery storage. For more information about ATMOCE and its energy storage technology, visit www.atmoce.com/au About ATMOCE Founded in 2024 and headquartered in Germany, ATMOCE is a global energy technology company committed to "Creating a Better World with Renewable Energy". ATMOCE develops integrated solar generation, energy storage and intelligent energy management technologies designed to help homeowners and businesses achieve greater energy independence. Through continuous innovation and a growing global partner ecosystem, ATMOCE is working to make renewable energy safer, smarter, simpler and more connected.
